title: Home Depot (HD) Beats Stock Market Upswing: What Investors Need to Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Home Depot closed at $286.69, outperforming the S&P 500 with a +1.97% daily gain. However, the stock has depreciated 12.43% over the past month, underperforming its sector. The company is expected to report earnings on November 17, 2026, with projected EPS of $3.86 (up 3.21% YoY) and quarterly revenue of $42.72 billion (up 3.3% YoY). Home Depot currently holds a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) and trades at a Forward P/E of 18.73, above its industry average of 16.8.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While HD outperformed the broader market on the trading day (+1.97% vs S&P 500's +0.58%), it has significantly underperformed over the past month (-12.43% vs sector's -4.5%). The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and trades at a premium valuation (Forward P/E of 18.73 vs industry average of 16.8). Modest earnings growth projections (3.21% EPS growth) and minimal estimate revisions (+0.07%) suggest limited near-term catalysts, warranting a neutral stance.

title: Home Depot (HD) Declines More Than Market: Some Information for Investors
author: Zacks.Com
description: Home Depot declined 1.23% on September 30, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500. The stock has fallen 9.92% over the past month. Upcoming Q3 earnings are expected on November 17, 2026, with projected EPS of $3.87 (up 3.48% YoY) and revenue of $42.72 billion (up 3.3% YoY). HD holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E of 19.2, but its PEG ratio of 3.17 exceeds the industry average of 1.93, suggesting the stock may be overvalued relative to growth prospects.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: HD declined 1.23% on the trading day and 9.92% over the past month, underperforming the S&P 500. While earnings growth projections are modest (3.48% EPS growth), the stock's PEG ratio of 3.17 significantly exceeds the industry average of 1.93, indicating potential overvaluation relative to growth. title: Which Value Stock Is the More Obvious Buy Now: Home Depot Under $310 a Share or Lowe's Under $200 a Share?
author: Lawrence Rothman, Cfa
description: Home Depot and Lowe's both trade at attractive valuations compared to their historical P/E ratios amid economic headwinds affecting the home-improvement retail sector. Home Depot's P/E ratio of 21 and stronger operational performance (1.7% same-store sales growth vs. Lowe's 0.2%) make it the more obvious value buy, as its larger scale should help it emerge stronger when economic conditions improve.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Better operational performance with 1.7% same-store sales growth and expanding gross margins (33.4% to 33.7%). P/E ratio of 21 is below its 10-year median of 23. Larger market size and economies of scale position it to outperform when economic conditions improve. Analyst favors it as the better value opportunity.

Trading at attractive valuation with P/E ratio of 16, down from 21-year median, but showing weaker operational performance with only 0.2% same-store sales growth and contracting gross margins (33.8% to 33%). While valuations are reasonable, operational momentum lags Home Depot, making it less favored as a value buy.
